rationale: Adults undergoing open cardiac surgery (OPCABG) with preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure were compared with non-users; outcomes included postoperative AKI and safety endpoints. Study design is original retrospective cohort with comparator.
eligibility_evidence: Methods 2.1 Study Population: consecutive OPCABG patients (age 18–80) 2018–2023; SGLT2i protocol: dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for ≥3 months preop, stopped 72 h before surgery; comparator: non-SGLT2i users with 1:3 PSM. rationale: Observational multicenter cohort of adults undergoing open cardiac surgery (CABG via MiECC). Exposure group was preoperative/ongoing SGLT2 inhibitor therapy (empagliflozin 10–25 mg daily for ≥6 months before CABG) compared with T2DM patients not on SGLT2i and a non-diabetic cohort. Reports clinical efficacy/safety outcomes (all-cause death, cardiac death, MI, stroke, repeat revascularization, composite) at 1 and 5 years.
eligibility_evidence: Methods: Adults >18 with multivessel CHD undergoing CABG via MiECC; T2DM patients classified as “SGLT2-I users” if they had used SGLT2i ≥6 months pre-CABG; empagliflozin 10 or 25 mg once daily (Materials and Methods). Comparator groups: T2DM non–SGLT2i users and non-T2DM (Table 1). Outcomes: all-cause death, cardiac death, non-fatal MI, stroke, repeat revascularization, composite endpoint at 1 and 5 years (Study Endpoints; Table 2).
